root_idea.summary: A covering or overlay that obscures what lies beneath.
root_idea.development: The root develops from physical covering, rust, and soiling to the obscuring or blackening of the heart, and further to states of being overcome, overwhelmed, or beset.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole supplied QAC group is an attested Form I verb with a distinct Quranic lexical use.

senses.definition: To cover or overcome the heart so that its clarity and discernment become obscured, like a layer of rust.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction رَانَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ, the covering is attributed to what people have been earning; it is explained as accumulated wrongdoing producing a rust-like covering or blackness that prevents recognition of good and evil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become rusty or covered with rust; hence, of cloth or a garment, to become dirty, filthy, or soiled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical coating or soiling use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the soul or stomach, to become heavy, agitated, or nauseated, with a tendency to vomit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction رَانَتْ نَفْسَهُ and related expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cover, overcome, overpower, or overwhelm a thing or person; to be beset by circumstances from which one cannot escape or cope, including debt, grief, wine, drowsiness, anxiety, or death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs with عَلَى, بِـ, or a direct object. The Quranic heart-and-wrongdoing construction is treated separately above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a people, for their cattle to perish or die, or to become lean and emaciated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV usage describing cattle overwhelmed by an event or loss.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of legging resembling a boot but longer and without a foot, traditionally described as cloth stuffed with cotton and worn beneath a boot in cold weather.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as an Arabicized Persian loan and explicitly characterized as not a genuine Arabic word.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rust or a coating that overspreads a sword, mirror, or other polished thing; also dirt, filth, pollution, or a covering, including the corresponding blackness or covering of the heart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for a physical layer or its figurative effect on the heart.
The name is explained by its overpowering the reason.
Used predicatively of a person who is surrounded or overtaken by something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: People whose cattle have perished or died, or whose cattle have become lean and emaciated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural designation for people afflicted by the loss or wasting of their cattle.
